_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::particles#10, and a falsification of its Signal. The rule holds — DOMAINBOUNDINGBOX must cover where the particles GO, not just where they start — but nothing aborts. Upstream particle_sph_2d_pdbody_gravity.4C.yaml is driven by gravity along +x; pulling the box's +x face in from 20.0 to 17.0 removes 120 outermost wall particles at setup and then, twice more while the body travels, deletes 3 particles at a time that were inside the box at t=0 and walked out of it. Those two mid-run events are exactly the motion-range effect the entry is about. The only trace is 'on processor 0 removed 3 particle(s) being outside the computational domain!', which names no id, no position, no step and no phase; the string 'particle out of domain' appears nowhere; and all 3001 evaluations still run, the same number as the healthy baseline, so there is no mid-run abort. The damage only surfaces at the very end as 8 wrong result values via core/utils/src/result_test/4C_utils_result_test.cpp line 181. A too-small box therefore does not stop a run: it silently deletes part of the model and hands back an answer. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.
expect_in_output: on processor 0 removed 120 particle(s) being outside the computational domain!
on processor 0 removed 3 particle(s) being outside the computational domain!

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: leave DOMAINBOUNDINGBOX at its upstream extent in the second arm. No particle ever leaves the box, all three removal events disappear, SMALLBOX_MIDRUN_REMOVAL_EVENTS becomes 0, SMALLBOX_FAILURES becomes 0 and EXIT_SMALLBOX becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
